safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes no neck stiffness, but there is no corresponding statement in the Generated Facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute, severe headache, documenting absence of neck stiffness is a key negative for meningitis/meningoencephalitis and other secondary headache causes. Omitting it may lead subsequent clinicians to assume it was not assessed, potentially prompting unnecessary escalation or incomplete risk stratification.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold notes no fever, but fever is not addressed in the Generated Facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is an important red-flag symptom in severe headache (e.g., infection/meningitis), and noting its absence helps contextualize urgency and differential diagnosis. Omission can impair continuity and may lead to additional evaluation or misinterpretation of infection risk.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states patient denies thoughts of self-harm; the Generated Facts do not include suicidality/self-harm denial.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Suicidal/self-harm ideation documentation is a safety-critical element when anxiety/depression is discussed; recording denial helps establish baseline risk and supports safe follow-up planning. Omission could lead to repeated assessments or uncertainty about safety screening having been performed.
